r1381.text: Opened Aldgate to the men of Kent and Essex against the mayor’s will.
Sent by Walworth to treat with the rebels; led their leaders into the city and entertained them at his house.
Let the rebels across London Bridge and refused help in defending it.
Rebels threw down the Temple in Fleet Street, then burned the Savoy.
The Savoy, John of Gaunt’s palace, looted and burned.
Houses broken into at Holborn, parish of St Andrew.

r1381.who: John Ferrour, Joanna his wife and others
r1381.text: Hospital of St John of Jerusalem at Clerkenwell burned; two horses loaded with wool carried off.
Archbishop Sudbury and Robert Hales, prior of St John, seized in the Tower and beheaded.
Came to the Guildhall with fire to burn the "Jubilee Book" of city ordinances.
Led rebels to the Compter in Milk Street, broke open chests searching for the Jubilee Book.
In Lombard Street displayed a standard and, claiming royal authority, disseised Richard Toky of his tenement and goods.
Seized Nicholas Brembre (grocer, former mayor) by the bridle at Aldgate as he rode with the king.
Took from the house of Reginald Aleyn at Walbrook a statute merchant (a registered debt bond) in which Raven himself was bound.
Expelled Nicholas Hawtot and family from his house by London Stone and forced him to hand over his tenements.
Went to the house of Hugh Fastolf in the parish of St Dunstan in the East (pardon).
Threatened to kill Andrew Vernoun, brewer, at Paul’s Wharf and pull down his house unless he paid a fine.
Indicted for killing three unnamed Flemings in London. The database gives no street; the Vintry placing follows the chronicle tradition and is mine.
Killed John Bochier, millward, on London Bridge by the Southwark end.
House in Walbrook ward entered; charters, deeds and court rolls burnt, valuables taken.
Left the king at Smithfield, rode to Aldgate and West Cheap, and stopped men there from going to his aid.
Confrontation at Smithfield; Wat Tyler killed. Horses of Robert Hales taken from a dealer’s premises the same day.
Houses of Robert Lyons and Robert Hardekyn plundered. The database gives no street; placed at Cheap.
Rebels accused before William Walworth’s commission held in Newgate.

trades.name: Gascon wine
trades.basis: Vintage fleet in late autumn and the "reek" fleet in spring (M. K. James, Studies in the Medieval Wine Trade). Wine was landed in the Vintry; whether large ships still passed the drawbridge in the fifteenth century needs checking.

trades.name: Wool to the staple (Flanders)
trades.basis: Wool customed at Wool Wharf and shipped in spring and autumn fleets; staple sites moved several times before 1363 (Lloyd, The English Wool Trade).

trades.name: Wool to the Calais staple
trades.basis: Staple fixed at Calais from 1363 (with interruptions); fleets often sailed in convoy.

trades.name: Cloth to the Brabant marts
trades.basis: Mercers and Merchant Adventurers shipping for the four marts of Antwerp and Bergen-op-Zoom (Easter, Whitsun, St Bavo, Cold). Timings to be checked (Sutton, The Mercery of London).

trades.name: Hanse cogs (Baltic)
trades.basis: Baltic navigation largely closed in winter; Hanse merchants landed at the Steelyard (Lloyd, England and the German Hanse).

trades.name: Stockfish (Bergen)
trades.basis: Norwegian stockfish via Bergen, a Hanse-dominated trade, chiefly in summer.

trades.name: Iceland voyages
trades.basis: English voyages to Iceland from the 1410s, mainly from East Anglia and Bristol; London’s share needs checking.

trades.name: Yarmouth herring
trades.basis: Yarmouth herring fair, Michaelmas to Martinmas.

trades.name: Sea-coal (Newcastle)
trades.basis: Coastal colliers, mostly in the sailing season.

trades.name: Italian galleys
trades.basis: Venetian Flanders galleys and Genoese carracks called mainly at Southampton; London calls (Galley Quay) need checking for frequency.

trades.name: Iberian trade
trades.basis: Castilian and Portuguese shipping (Childs, Anglo-Castilian Trade).

trades.name: Low Countries goods
trades.basis: Year-round short-sea traffic; cf. the Dordrecht cog of 1389.

trades.name: Coastal corn
trades.basis: East Anglian and Kentish grain to Queenhithe and Billingsgate, peaking after harvest.
